Cloud-sea stretching to a copper-amber horizon at sunset, the curve of the earth faintly suggested at the far edge, all distance and dissolving light.
Gas-lit Victorian London receding far below, the Thames a silver thread through amber fog, church spires barely piercing the lantern-glow haze.
Thunderhead wall building to the west, lightning forking silently inside the bruised mass, ten miles distant and visibly closing.
Distant Himalayan peaks rising from a cloud-floor at dawn, all blue-haze recession and cold altitude, far beyond the airship rigging.
Constantinople's minarets piercing the golden haze below, the Bosphorus a pale ribbon, the whole city softened to watercolor in afternoon atmosphere.
Sister-airships in loose formation off the starboard quarter, half-swallowed by cloud-haze, their envelopes faint silver oblongs against a bruised sky.
Sahara dunes rolling under late-afternoon copper haze, the low sun bleeding orange across the ridgelines, all distance and baked silence.
Full moon rising over a silver cloud-sea, the light pooling in every hollow, the horizon dissolving into luminous pale nothing.
Patagonian glaciers catching cold blue light far below through shredding cloud, their crevasse-shadows ink-dark, the whole range half-veiled in altitude haze.
Enemy dirigible-armada looming on the eastern horizon, their silhouettes ranked in grey atmospheric recession, still distant but unmistakably purposeful.
Cairo pyramids dissolving into golden desert haze below, the Nile barely a thread, the whole ancient geometry softened by afternoon atmospheric depth.
Above the anvil of a spent thundercloud, its flat top lit rose-gold by the sun, the sky above deepening to violet infinity.
Andean condor-country far below in blue-grey haze, the mountain flanks falling into shadow-filled valleys, distance reducing all detail to texture.
Blizzard-front advancing from the north, a white wall erasing the horizon mile by mile, the air ahead already flickering with driven snow.
Tokyo Bay shimmering far below through evening haze, its water hammered to pale pewter, the distant shore reduced to a grey smear.
Golden-hour cloudtops stretching in every direction, lit amber and rose from below, the shadows between them pooling in deep indigo.
Dirigible-armada at anchor above a cloud-floor, their mooring cables descending into haze, their running-lights beginning to glow in the thickening dusk.
Sandstorm pillar turning slowly on the desert horizon below, its base lost in ochre murk, its crown feathering against a pale brass sky.
Above a solid overcast at midnight, the cloud-sea utterly white under the moon, the horizon a clean ruled line between silver and black.
Scandinavian fjords slicing the coastline far below through cold Atlantic haze, the water dark between pale cliff-walls, all detail smoothed by distance.
Lightning-laced cloud-wall to the south, the discharges illuminating the interior in stuttering cold-white pulses, the whole mass in slow churning motion.
Great barrier-reef shallows visible far below through tropical haze, the water shifting from deep blue to impossible turquoise, distance bleeding all edges soft.
Sister-airship running parallel a half-mile off, her hull dark against sunset, her envelope catching the last copper light, rigging just-visible in the haze.
Serengeti plain unrolling far below under dusty afternoon haze, the great herds invisible at this altitude, the land a patchwork of amber and ochre.
Aurora curtains rippling across the polar sky ahead, green and pale violet shifting in slow waves, the cloud-sea below reflecting their cold fire.
